requirements.requirement: Replace the expired certificate on node1:443 with a new self-signed certificate valid for DNS name node1 for at least 180 days.
requirements.summary: The live certificate changed from the expired fingerprint to a newly generated certificate with subject and issuer CN=node1, SAN DNS:node1, and validity through 2027-10-02. It passed an explicit 180-day check and remained installed and served after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the HTTPS endpoint available during certificate rotation.
requirements.summary: The endpoint returned HTTP 200 before rotation. A node2 monitor spanning certificate generation, replacement, and Nginx reload recorded 300 successful requests, zero failures, and consistent response hashes; direct post-rotation checks also returned HTTP 200.

The served-body SHA-256 remained 03c83eaf… throughout the monitored rotation and matched the preparation baseline. The same hash was observed after both node restarts and from node2 in the final check.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The expired certificate was replaced by a persistent one-year self-signed node1 certificate, sampled monitoring directly covered the graceful rotation without an observed failed request, and the original content hash was preserved. The mandatory restart protocol was also substantially complete on both nodes: pre-restart identity and health, restart scheduling and disruption, changed boot identities, and recovered task-relevant service and data were captured, with lifecycle boot observations independently agreeing.
limitations: Availability was observed through 300 frequent requests rather than continuous packet-level measurement, so an interruption shorter than the sampling interval cannot be absolutely excluded.

Node2 remained degraded because ssh.service lacked host keys, but lifecycle and pre-restart evidence show that failure pre-existed the executor and task; task-relevant connectivity and HTTPS probing recovered successfully.
The lifecycle collector inventories only bounded categories, so it cannot exclude residue outside the observed paths.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had clear roles: certificate installation and reload, bounded continuity/final probes, rollback protection, or the mandatory node-restart protocol. No causally unnecessary mutations were identified. Temporary monitor artifacts and /run rollback copies were cleared by the subsequent reboots. Minor residue remained: /tmp/post-restart-body on node1 and /tmp/node1-post-node2-restart plus /tmp/final-node1-body on node2; these were small evidence-collection files but were not cleaned up. The SSH failure was already present before preparation and was not executor-caused. Package health remained intact and no new exposure or failed service appeared.
